plan.notes: True degree name: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science (BS in Computer Science), School of Computing, Thomas J. Watson College of Engineering and Applied Science. Term-by-term sequence transcribed verbatim from the official School of Computing sample 4-year schedule ('No Waiver for CS 110, Calculus Ready' variant; labeled for students entering Fall 2023 through Spring 2027), the 'No Waiver' variant being the complete default freshman path; a parallel official 'Waiver for CS 110, Calculus Ready' variant exists in the same PDF for students granted a CS 110 waiver by the Undergraduate Director. Minimum 126 credit hours per the official 'Requirements for Bachelor of Science in Computer Science' (students matriculated Fall 2023 or after, https://www.binghamton.edu/watson/student-services/advising/undergrad-forms/cs-2023.pdf), verified against the 2025-2026 Binghamton University Academic Guide (bulletin.binghamton.edu), which publishes the same 126-credit minimum -- catalog_year recorded as 2025-2026. Transcription method: manual transcription of the official PDF schedule into term slots; credit ranges in the source were resolved to one coherent 126-credit path (sophomore-fall science-sequence lab taken (2 cr) + free elective 2 cr; senior-fall free elective 2 cr; senior-spring free elective 4 cr), with the catalog alternatives documented in choice_notes. Course-level prerequisites are NOT stated in the sample schedule itself; prereq arrays encode the official prerequisites table from the Fall-2023+ requirements handout. Validator-mapping decisions (no invented codes): where an official prereq names a course option inside a choice slot, the prereq points at the slot's own code -- 'MATH 224/225' for the official MATH 225, 'MATH 226/227' for the official MATH 226/227, 'MATH-CHOICE-1' for the official MATH 314/330 alternative. CS 110's official prereq MATH 225 may be taken concurrently (footnote 1) and is scheduled here in the same Fall Year 1 term. CS 301's official table entry also lists a Gen Ed C/J course and CS 220 or CS 310 (either); the sample schedule places CS 301 in the same term as CS 220, so its prereq array encodes only CS 101 and the remainder is documented here. Footnotes carried from the source: (0) CS 110 counts as free-elective credit and is not counted in the 52 CS credits; (2) the science sequence is CHEM 104/105/106 or 107/108 (10 or 8 cr), BIOL 113/114/115 (10 cr), or PHYS 131/132 (8 cr), and the total of science + free-elective credits (blocks 3 and 6) should be 22; (4) students take one MATH course per semester after calculus to obtain prerequisites for 300-level CS classes; (5/6) five 3-credit CS electives (15 cr) chosen across breadth areas A-E with at least one course from each of areas A, B, C and at most one from area E. Placement prerequisites documented here, not encoded: students not placing into MATH 224 take MATH 223 (or equivalent) and, if needed, MATH 108/107/106; underprepared students may need CHEM 100 before CHEM 104/105/106; CS 110 is required unless the student is placed into CS 120/210 via prior programming experience (Undergraduate Director waiver).
